hypotheses.name: malignant pleural mesothelioma
hypotheses.basis: Diffuse, nodular, circumferential pleural thickening with mediastinal invasion and contralateral pleural involvement is highly characteristic of epithelioid or biphasic mesothelioma; absence of discrete lung mass favors pleural primary over metastatic carcinoma

hypotheses.name: metastatic pleural disease (e.g., from lung or breast cancer)
hypotheses.basis: Nodular pleural thickening can occur in metastases; however, the diffuse, rind-like encasement and bilateral involvement are more typical of mesothelioma; requires histopathology for distinction

hypotheses.name: pleural infection (e.g., tuberculous empyema with fibrosis)
hypotheses.basis: Can cause pleural thickening, but typically less nodular and less aggressive mediastinal impingement; no associated cavitation or lymphadenopathy seen here
